body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The public API functions (getEntry, getSingleEntry, getSingletonEntry, findSingletonEntry) do not accept or propagate the `includeDraft` flag. While `ICreateQueryConfig` and `ICreateEntryConfig` have the field, the public interfaces `IContentstackGetEntry`, `IContentstackGetSingleEntry`, and `IContentstackGetSingletonEntry` do not include `includeDraft`, and none of the public functions pass it through to the factory. The flag is unreachable from any call site — the feature is dead code.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `includeDraft?: boolean` to `IContentstackGetEntry` (and by extension its descendants). In each public function (getEntry, getSingleEntry, getSingletonEntry, findSingletonEntry), destructure `includeDraft` and pass it through to `factory.createContentTypeQuery({ ..., includeDraft })` / `createContentTypeEntryQuery({ ..., includeDraft })`.

issues.description: No `getStaticProps` integration found — search for `context.preview` / `previewData` returned zero matches across the entire `src/` tree. The prescribed fix requires propagating `context.preview` from Next.js getStaticProps through to the factory methods. Without this, no page can ever activate draft mode, so all three acceptance criteria fail: draft content will never be served in preview, and the 'update without rebuild' criterion is untestable.
issues.suggestedFix: In each page's getStaticProps (or a shared getStaticProps helper), read `context.preview` (and/or `context.previewData`) and pass `includeDraft: !!context.preview` through to the content-fetching calls (getEntry/getSingleEntry/getSingletonEntry/findSingletonEntry).

issues.description: Uses `query.addParam("include_draft", "true")` instead of the Contentstack SDK's native `query.includeDraft()` method as prescribed. The SDK's `.includeDraft()` is the documented, supported mechanism for draft content retrieval and may perform additional internal logic beyond a raw param. Hand-rolling the param is both a deviation from the prescribed fix and a fragility risk if the SDK changes its internal param naming.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace `query.addParam("include_draft", "true")` with `query.includeDraft()` in both `createContentTypeQuery` and `createContentTypeEntryQuery`.

issues.description: Stack initialization reads `live_preview` config from env vars only (management_token + host). The prescribed fix requires also reading preview hash, content_type_uid, and uid from request query params (provided by the Contentstack Live Preview SDK). Without these runtime params, the SDK cannot correlate the preview session with the correct draft entry, so live preview updates (AC #2: 'updates without requiring a rebuild') will not work.
issues.suggestedFix: Integrate the Live Preview SDK's `live_preview` config to accept runtime query params (preview_hash/content_type_uid/entry_uid). This typically involves passing request query params through to the Stack or using the Contentstack Live Preview SDK's `getLivePreview` / middleware to inject them.

issues.description: No unit tests found for the contentstack service — no test file mirrors `src/services/contentstack`. The review criteria require new features to have corresponding vitest unit tests in test/unit/ mirroring the src/ path. None of the three verification criteria (draft in preview, update without rebuild, published outside preview) are covered by tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `test/unit/services/contentstack.test.ts` with tests verifying: (1) when `includeDraft` is true, the query calls `.includeDraft()` (or equivalent); (2) when `includeDraft` is false/absent, `.includeDraft()` is NOT called; (3) the public functions propagate `includeDraft` through to the factory. Mock the Stack/Query to assert the call.

issues.description: In `createContentTypeQuery`, `query.toJSON()` is called immediately after the `includeDraft` check but BEFORE `setCommonConfig`, `where`, `skip`, `limit`, and `count` are applied. The original code had `toJSON()` before these too, but the ordering means `includeDraft()` (or addParam) is called before `toJSON()`. If the SDK's `.includeDraft()` must be chained after `.toJSON()`, this could silently fail. Verify SDK documentation for correct chaining order.
issues.suggestedFix: Verify the Contentstack SDK's expected method chaining order. If `.includeDraft()` should be called after `.toJSON()`, move it. If order doesn't matter, add a comment confirming this.

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The `includeDraft` flag is added to `ICreateQueryConfig` and `ICreateEntryConfig` and handled inside `ContentstackFactory`, but none of the public-facing functions (`getEntry`, `getSingleEntry`, `getSingletonEntry`, `getSingletonEntry`) accept or propagate `includeDraft` to the factory. Then in each public function (`getEntry`, `getSingleEntry`, `getSingletonEntry`, `getSingletonEntry`), pass `includeDraft` from the function args into the factory call: `factory.createContentTypeQuery({ ..., includeDraft })` and `factory.createContentTypeEntryQuery({ ..., includeDraft })`.

issues.description: No page-level `getStaticProps` (or any caller) passes `context.preview` through to the contentstack service calls. The prescribed fix states: 'Propagate preview flag from getStaticProps context (context.preview) through to these factory methods.' This propagation is entirely missing — no page reads `context.preview` and passes `includeDraft: true` to `getEntry`/`getSingleEntry`/`getSingletonEntry`. Without this, the CMS preview experience will never display draft content.
issues.suggestedFix: In each page's `getStaticProps`, read `context.preview` and pass `includeDraft: Boolean(context.preview)` to the contentstack service calls. Alternatively, create a shared helper (e.g. in `services/contentstack.ts`) that wraps the preview flag extraction from Next.js context.

issues.description: No vitest unit tests were added for the live preview / includeDraft functionality. The diff only modifies existing test files (removing date/insertDate assertions from unrelated email-sign-up tests). There are zero tests verifying that `includeDraft: true` causes `addParam('include_draft', 'true')` to be called, or that `includeDraft: false`/omitted does not. Per review criteria, new features must have corresponding vitest unit tests mirroring the src/ path.
issues.suggestedFix: Add `src/__tests__/services/contentstack.spec.ts` (or similar) with tests that: (1) mock the Stack and verify `addParam('include_draft', 'true')` is called when `includeDraft` is passed; (2) verify it is NOT called when omitted; (3) verify the `live_preview` config is applied to the Stack when env vars are present.

issues.description: The `query.toJSON()` call is now separated from the query chain and its return value is discarded. In the original code, `.toJSON()` was chained and returned the query for further chaining. Now `query.toJSON()` is called as a standalone statement (line 153/155), and subsequent calls like `query.includeCount()`, `query.skip()`, `query.where()` operate on the original query object. While this may work if the SDK mutates in place, the discarded return value is fragile and differs from the SDK's intended fluent API usage. If `.toJSON()` returns a new wrapper, subsequent calls won't take effect.
issues.suggestedFix: Reorder so `.toJSON()` is called last (after all param additions), or capture its return: `const query = this.stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Query().language(lang); if (includeDraft) query.addParam('include_draft', 'true'); ... return query.toJSON();` — ensuring `.toJSON()` is the terminal call returning the final query object.

issues.description: A new `KB.md` file is added under `orchestrations/agents/` which appears to be agent orchestration metadata, not project source code. This file should not be committed to the repository as it is tooling artifact, not application code.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove `orchestrations/agents/KB.md` from the commit or add it to `.gitignore`.

issues.description: Security: CONTENTSTACK_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN is passed to the client-side and used in the browser via process.env inside a client component. Management tokens are sensitive credentials that must never be exposed to the browser bundle. Next.js inlines process.env references at build time, so this token will be embedded in client-side JavaScript.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a server-side API route (e.g., /api/preview-content) that holds the management token server-side and returns preview content. The client-side provider should call this API endpoint instead of creating a Stack directly with credentials.

issues.description: Only the 'page' content field is updated by fetchLivePreviewContent. setLiveContent merges with defaultContent but only overrides page. If a CMS edit targets header, footer, serviceAlerts, globalDictionary, or any other content type, the preview will not reflect those changes. Acceptance criterion 'on-screen components that render that content — headings, body text, and images from the edited entry — display the updated values' is only partially met.
issues.suggestedFix: Use the content_type_uid from the preview params to determine which content slice to update, and merge the fetched entry into the correct field of the content object (e.g., if content_type_uid is 'header', update content.header).

issues.description: No vitest unit tests were added for the live preview functionality. Per review criteria, new features must have corresponding vitest unit tests in test/unit/ mirroring the src/ path. There are zero tests verifying: (a) that previewConfig.enable=true activates live preview fetching, (b) that hashchange triggers re-fetch, (c) that non-preview mode falls back to defaultContent, (d) that getLivePreviewParams correctly parses hash params.
issues.suggestedFix: Add test/unit/context/ContentstackContext.test.tsx with vitest tests covering: initial state matches defaultContent, setContent updates context and triggers re-render, preview mode activates live fetching, non-preview mode uses static content, hashchange event triggers re-fetch.

issues.description: A new contentstack.Stack() instance is created inside fetchLivePreviewContent on every invocation, including every hashchange event. This is inefficient, may leak resources, and is not the prescribed approach. The prescribed fix states to register the Stack.livePreview callback (via Stack.livePreview.onContentUpdate) once, which then calls setContent with updated content — no per-event Stack creation needed.
issues.suggestedFix: Create the Stack instance once (e.g., in a useRef or module scope) and register the SDK's live preview callback (Stack.livePreview.onContentUpdate) to call setLiveContent. Use the hashchange listener only as a fallback if the SDK callback is unavailable.

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: The ContentstackProvider calls applyLivePreviewQuery() on hashchange/message events but NEVER re-fetches content and NEVER calls setContent with new data. applyLivePreviewQuery only calls Stack.livePreviewQuery() which sets internal SDK state — nothing triggers a new Stack query or updates the React context. The setContent(defaultContent) effect only fires when the defaultContent prop changes (page navigation), not on hashchange. Therefore the UI will never display draft/preview content. This fails all three acceptance criteria: (1) modified draft content is never displayed during a live-preview session, (2) the published version is shown not because of correct fallback logic but because live preview is entirely non-functional, and (3) subsequent edits never appear without a page reload because no re-fetch mechanism exists. The prescribed minimal fix explicitly states: 'call the Stack query again with Stack.livePreviewQuery() applied, and setContent with the result.' The diff omits the critical re-fetch and setContent steps.
issues.suggestedFix: Inside the hashchange/message handler, after calling applyLivePreviewQuery(), re-fetch the page content via the existing Stack query functions (e.g., getEntry or getSingleEntry) and call setContent with the result. For example: const liveContent = await getEntry({ contentTypeUid: content_type_uid, lang: currentLocale, ... }); setContent(prev => ({ ...prev, [content_type_uid]: liveContent }));

issues.description: The 'message' event listener calls handleHashChange which only reads window.location.hash — it does not read event.data. A postMessage from the Contentstack editor does not change window.location.hash, so the handler will re-parse the same hash and do nothing. The comment says 'Contentstack's editor posts a message on preview; re-parse on receipt' but the implementation cannot deliver real-time updates via this mechanism. Contentstack's Live Preview SDK uses postMessage/WebSocket for real-time content updates, not URL hash changes. Relying solely on hashchange may miss updates that don't change the hash, failing AC3: 'subsequent content edits made in the CMS appear in the rendered UI without requiring a full page reload.'
issues.suggestedFix: Either (a) register the Contentstack SDK's built-in live preview callback (e.g., Stack.livePreview.onContentUpdate or equivalent) to trigger a re-fetch and setContent, or (b) if using the message listener, parse event.data for the preview payload (not window.location.hash) and re-fetch content accordingly. The current approach of re-reading window.location.hash on a message event cannot work.

issues.description: Untyped 'any' cast: (Stack as any).livePreviewQuery({ live_preview, content_type_uid }) has no explanatory comment. Per review criteria, no untyped 'any' without an explanatory comment. The file has a top-level eslint-disable for no-explicit-any but the review criteria require an inline comment explaining why 'any' is necessary here.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an inline comment explaining the cast (e.g., '// contentstack 3.17.2 types do not expose livePreviewQuery on the Stack interface') or extend the contentstack module augmentation to declare livePreviewQuery on the Stack type.

issues.description: catch (e: any) uses untyped 'any' for the catch parameter. Per TypeScript strict compliance, catch parameters should be typed as 'unknown' and narrowed. The code then accesses e?.message which is unsafe on 'any' and would be type-checked on 'unknown'.

issues.description: When CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_ENABLE is not 'true' or CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN is missing, live preview is silently disabled with no warning or error logged. The existing code logs errors for missing CONTENTSTACK_API_KEY, CONTENTSTACK_DELIVERY_TOKEN, CONTENTSTACK_ENVIRONMENT, and CONTENTSTACK_BRANCH, but there is no equivalent warning for the missing preview configuration. An operator or editor will see published content with no indication that draft preview is unavailable.

Per TypeScript strict compliance criteria, no untyped any is allowed without a comment explaining why. The Contentstack SDK types may not expose livePreviewQuery, but the cast should be documented.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an explanatory comment (e.g., '// Contentstack SDK types do not expose livePreviewQuery; cast required') or extend the module augmentation for the contentstack types.
